dedupe_keys.name: la metro bus stop prioritization analysis 2024 scores for 12 003 bus stops including tree canopy and urban heat

description: A GIS scoring of every bus stop served by the Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority, made in 2024 to show cities which stops most need shade, lighting and other improvements. Contents: 12,003 stops, each scored from 0 to 100 on nine weighted criteria, with a list of the 1,200 highest-scoring critical need stops. The criteria are Metro Equity Focus Communities, CalEnviroScreen disadvantaged communities, vulnerable populations from the 2021 American Community Survey, the CalEPA Urban Heat Island Index, tree canopy (stops with no canopy within 50 feet, from the 2018 EarthDefine canopy layer built on NAIP imagery and USGS lidar), the SCAG high injury network, historical redlining, air toxics cancer risk and ridership. Coverage: Los Angeles County, as a March 2024 snapshot; as of 2022 only 24% of stops in the county had shelters. Format and access: maps for each criterion are viewable on the Bus Stop Hub; shapefiles, KMZ and CSV files for the ten analyses and an explainer are sent on request by email. Licence and cost: free; no licence is stated. Caveats: one agency's weighting, a snapshot, and inputs of different dates. Useful for heat exposure and adaptation studies of people waiting at stops, and for choosing where shelters or trees cut heat stress. It relates to the Austin bus stop shelter and tree shade ridership study in the catalogue.
